newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes higher on dollar squaring.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes higher on dollar squaring.

text.p: The won ended slightly higher against the dollar on Thursday as banks squared their long dollar positions, dealers said.
The won stood at 828.90 at the close after opening at 829.30. It moved in a range of 828.80 to 830.40.
Many banks unloaded their dollars in the afternoon upon realising the market was not short on dollars. They had bought dollars as the market was rumoured to be lacking the U.S. unit.
"When the dollar failed to rise much above 830, banks started to get rid of their long dollar holdings," said one local trader.
The won is expected to move in a range of 828.00 to 829.30 on Friday. The central bank set the base mid-rate for Friday at 828.90 unchanged from Thursday.
